data.name: Olwen
data.gender_notes: Olwen is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Olwen is a Welsh name derived from the Old Welsh word 'olwen', which means 'white sheen' or 'fawn'. In Welsh mythology, Olwen was the name of a beautiful maiden who was said to be the cause of the magic of the flowers in the Garden of Rhos. She was also the name of a fairy queen who was known for her beauty, grace, and power.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of new beginnings, purity, and grace.
data.etymology: Olwen belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fawn.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Olwen total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_greek.name: Όλβεν
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Όλβεν έχει τις ρίζες του στην κελτική και ελληνική παράδοση. Στην ελληνική, η λέξη 'Όλβ' σχετίζεται με την έννοια της ευτυχίας και της λάμψης. in_latin.name: Olwen

in_english.name: Olwen
in_english.long_meaning: The name Olwen originates from Celtic and Christian traditions. It is derived from the Welsh name 'Olwen', which means 'God is my eternal light' or 'track of the lamb'. The name signifies a deep connection with God and spiritual light. Historically, Olwen is associated with Saint Olwen, a 5th-century Welsh saint. The name symbolizes guidance, hope, and divine presence in one's life.
